members.subtitle: People who can sign in to manage this business.

invite.bodyGeneric: You've been invited to join a business on VoiceDesk.

account.title: Account
account.twoFactorOn: On — you'll be asked for a code from your authenticator app when you sign in.
account.twoFactorOff: Off. We strongly recommend turning it on.
account.setupUri: Add this key to your authenticator app (paste the link or enter it manually):

account.nameHint: Shown to your team. When you take a call in the VA console, the caller hears your first name ("You're through to Sam now").
account.name: Full name
account.passwordHint: Use at least 10 characters. Passwords found in known data breaches aren't allowed.
account.signOutOthers: Sign out on all my other devices
account.sessionsHint: Sign out any device you don't recognise, then change your password. Sessions end after 7 days without use.

knowledge.title: Knowledge
knowledge.subtitle: What your assistant knows about the business. Add your website, documents and FAQs.
knowledge.crawlNotice: We'll read public pages on this site (respecting robots.txt) and re-check weekly. Only add websites you own or have permission to use.
knowledge.fileHint: PDF, Word (DOCX), CSV or text, up to 20 MB.
knowledge.empty: Nothing added yet. Start with your website.
knowledge.stats: {documents, plural, one {# page} other {# pages}}, {chunks} passages
knowledge.testSubtitle: Ask a question a customer might ask and see which passages would be used to answer.

profile.title: Business profile
profile.subtitle: The facts your assistant can state with confidence. Generate a draft from your knowledge, check it carefully, then approve it. Only the approved version is used with customers.
profile.notLive: Not approved yet — the assistant has no business facts
profile.generated: A new draft was generated from your knowledge. Review it before approving.
profile.generateTimeout: Generation is taking longer than expected. Refresh the page in a minute.
profile.approvedNotice: Approved. The assistant now uses this profile.
profile.aiUnavailable: AI generation is off because no AI provider is switched on (Platform admin → AI providers). You can still fill in the profile by hand.
profile.faqsHint: Questions and answers the assistant can use word for word. Add your own here.
profile.question: Question
profile.salesHint: This is what lets the assistant complete conversations on its own: recommending the right service and getting people booked or signed up.
profile.primaryGoal: What should a successful conversation end in?
profile.whoWeServe: Who you serve (ages, eligibility, customer types)
profile.newCustomerSteps: How a new customer signs up / enrols
profile.bufferHint: Minutes kept free between appointments, 0 to 240 (for example 10).

agent.title: Assistant
agent.subtitle: Choose how your AI assistant sounds and which languages it speaks. It always tells customers it's an AI.
agent.personaHint: Each persona has its own tone. You can give it a different name.
agent.languagesHint: The assistant replies in the customer's language when it's enabled here.

console.title: Test console
console.subtitle: Talk to your assistant exactly as a customer would. Records it creates here are real, so you can check the whole flow.
console.noProfile: No business profile is approved yet, so the assistant knows nothing about the business. Approve a profile first for realistic answers.

records.title: Records
records.subtitle: Customers, bookings, complaints and messages your assistant has handled.
records.gapsHint: Add the answer to your business profile (FAQs) or knowledge, so the assistant can answer it next time without involving anyone.
records.noGaps: None. The assistant has answered everything it was asked.
records.confirmCancel: Cancel this booking? It's removed from your calendar and the customer gets a cancellation text.
records.aiCallHint: The assistant phones the customer back during calling hours (8am–9pm) from your number. Calls cost money at your phone provider.

platform.title: Platform admin
platform.subtitle: Choose which AI models power VoiceDesk for every business. Switched-on providers are tried in this order; if one fails, the next takes over. Changes apply within about 10 seconds.
platform.noEncryption: SETTINGS_ENCRYPTION_KEY is missing from .env, so API keys can't be stored. Add it and restart.
platform.noneActive: No AI provider is switched on and ready. The assistant is using the offline mock.
platform.keyOptional: Not needed for most local servers
platform.thinkLive: Let it think during live conversations (slower)
platform.thinkBackground: Let it think for background work

voice.agentMissing: The voice assistant hasn't joined. Check that the voice agent is running and the LiveKit, Deepgram and ElevenLabs keys are set in .env.
voice.connectFailed: Couldn't connect the call. Check your microphone permission and try again.
voice.latencyHint: Per reply, in milliseconds: end of your speech → reply text → first audio. Target: median under 800 ms.
voice.previewUnavailable: Voice preview needs an ElevenLabs key in .env.
voice.recordCallsHint: Adds a short recording notice to the greeting. Transcripts are always kept.
voice.fillerHint: * The assistant said “Just a moment” while it looked something up; the full answer came later.

calls.title: Calls
calls.subtitle: Every call your assistant has taken, with transcripts, summaries and recordings.
calls.noNumber: No phone number yet. Your VoiceDesk administrator assigns one; meanwhile you can test by voice in the Test console.
calls.forwardTitle: Keep your existing number: forward calls here
calls.forwardIntro: On most UK landlines and mobiles, dial one of these from the phone you want to forward:
calls.forwardNote: Codes vary by network and phone system (some business lines set this in an online portal). To cancel, dial ##21#, ##61# or ##67#. Your provider may charge for forwarded calls.
calls.latencyHint: From the end of the caller's speech to the assistant's first audio, across {turns} replies in {calls} calls. Target: median under 800 ms.
calls.recordingHint: Caller on the left channel, assistant on the right. Keep recordings only as long as you need them.
calls.noSummary: No summary yet. It's written a few seconds after the call ends.
calls.whileWithPerson: said while talking to a person
calls.handoffReturned: Then handed back to the assistant.
calls.aiCallsHint: Callbacks customers asked for and booking confirmations. Placed between 8am and 9pm, at most twice each.

phoneNumbers.title: Phone numbers
phoneNumbers.subtitle: Numbers bought in Twilio or Telnyx and the business each one rings. Calls are answered by that business's assistant.
phoneNumbers.notConfigured: LiveKit isn't configured (LIVEKIT_URL, LIVEKIT_API_KEY, LIVEKIT_API_SECRET in .env), so numbers can't be routed.
phoneNumbers.addHint: Buy the number at the carrier first and point its calls at LiveKit (see the setup steps below). Adding it here creates the LiveKit routing.
phoneNumbers.label: Label
phoneNumbers.confirmRemove: Remove this number? Calls to it will stop being answered. Release it at the carrier separately if you no longer need it.
phoneNumbers.twilioSetup1: Set SIP_AUTH_USERNAME and SIP_AUTH_PASSWORD in .env (Twilio sends them with each call; LiveKit rejects calls without them).
phoneNumbers.twilioSetup2: Twilio → TwiML Bins: create a bin that dials sip:+44…@YOUR-LIVEKIT-SIP-HOST;transport=tcp with that username and password (see the README).
phoneNumbers.twilioSetup3: Phone Numbers → your number → Voice: "A call comes in" → TwiML Bin → choose the bin.
phoneNumbers.telnyxSetup1: Telnyx → Voice → SIP Trunking: create an FQDN connection to your LiveKit SIP host, port 5060, TCP, number format +E.164, inbound region Europe.
phoneNumbers.telnyxSetup2: Numbers: buy a UK number (Telnyx checks ID and a UK address first, about 3 days) and assign it to that connection.
phoneNumbers.telnyxSetup3: Choose Telnyx as the carrier when adding it here. Its route only accepts calls from Telnyx's servers.
phoneNumbers.setupLast: Add the number here, assign it to a business, then call it.

integrations.title: Integrations
integrations.subtitle: Connect the tools your business already uses, so the assistant works with them.

result.connected: Calendar connected. Now choose which calendar bookings go into.
result.failed: The calendar service didn't accept the connection. Please try again.
result.no_refresh_token: The calendar service didn't grant ongoing access. Remove VoiceDesk from your account's connected apps, then connect again.

integrations.notConfigured: No calendar service is set up on this VoiceDesk server yet (the administrator needs to add Google or Microsoft app credentials).
integrations.askOwner: An owner or admin can connect a calendar.
integrations.pickToFinish: Choose a calendar to finish. Until then, the assistant only uses VoiceDesk's own bookings.
integrations.howItWorks: Busy times in this calendar are blocked; new bookings appear here with the customer's name, phone and reference. Your customers aren't sent calendar invitations; VoiceDesk sends its own confirmations.
integrations.errorHelp: The last attempt to reach your calendar failed. The assistant is still taking bookings and will use your calendar again when it responds.
integrations.revokedHelp: Access to your calendar was removed or has expired. Reconnect so the assistant can see your diary again; until then it only uses VoiceDesk's own bookings.
integrations.confirmDisconnect: Disconnect this calendar? The assistant will stop checking it and stop adding bookings to it. Existing events stay in your calendar.
integrations.calendarHint: Connect the calendar your business already uses. The assistant only offers times that are free in it, and puts every booking it makes straight into it.

contacts.title: Contacts
contacts.subtitle: Your customers. The assistant recognises callers by their number and adds new people when they book, sign up or leave a message.
contacts.importHint: Upload a CSV file (from Excel, Google Sheets or your old system) with names and phone numbers or emails. Up to 5,000 rows.
contacts.fileTooBig: That file is too large. Split it into files under 3 MB.
contacts.rowsFound: {count, plural, one {# row} other {# rows}} found. Check which column is which:
contacts.tooManyRows: More than {max} rows; split the file.

field.doNotCall: Don't phone this person (they asked not to be called)

contacts.import: Import {count, plural, one {# row} other {# rows}}
contacts.imported: {created} added, {updated} updated{errors, plural, =0 {.} one {, # row skipped:} other {, # rows skipped:}}
contacts.empty: No contacts yet. They appear when callers book or leave details, or import your existing customers above.
contacts.confirmDelete: Delete this contact? Their calls, bookings and messages stay, but are no longer linked to them. This can't be undone.

notifications.title: Confirmations, reminders and alerts
notifications.hint: Messages the assistant sends after it books, moves or cancels, and how your team hears about urgent problems.
notifications.confirmationsHint: A short text (and an email, if they gave one) when a booking is made, moved or cancelled, in the language they spoke.
notifications.alertPhoneHint: Urgent problems, callback requests and urgent messages are emailed to owners and admins straight away. Add a mobile to get a text too.

transfers.title: Putting callers through (phone calls)
transfers.hint: When a caller asks to speak to someone, the assistant can connect them to a person instead of taking a message: someone at the VA console in their browser (with the conversation so far on screen), or a phone number.
transfers.transferPhone: Number to put callers through to
transfers.urgentPlaceholder: e.g. burst pipe, no heating, gas smell
transfers.note: Leave the number empty to always take a message instead. Life-threatening emergencies are always told to call 999. Transferred calls are charged by your phone provider.
transfers.routePeopleThenPhone: VA console first, then the phone number
transfers.routeHint: The VA console rings people who answer calls for you (Team page) and are set to Available.
transfers.ringSeconds: Seconds the VA console rings before giving up

websiteChat.title: Website chat
websiteChat.subtitle: Put your assistant on your website. Visitors chat with it like on the phone: it answers questions, books, takes messages and signs people up.
websiteChat.statusHint: While it's off, the chat button doesn't appear even if the snippet is on your site.
websiteChat.whereHint: Only these websites can show your chat (one per line). This stops other sites copying your snippet.
websiteChat.snippetHint: Paste this just before the closing body tag on every page (or in your website builder's "custom code" setting).
websiteChat.confirmRegenerate: Create a new key? The current snippet stops working until you replace it on your website.
websiteChat.previewOff: Turn the chat on to preview it here.

inbox.title: Inbox
inbox.subtitle: Every customer conversation from your website chat, WhatsApp, email and forms. The assistant answers; you can step in at any time.
inbox.replyTakesOver: Write a reply (this takes over from the assistant)…
inbox.noEmail: This customer didn't leave an email address. Call them back instead.

whatsapp.subtitle: Customers message your business on WhatsApp; the assistant answers in the same way as on the phone and website, and you can take over from the Inbox.
whatsapp.notConnectedHint: Your VoiceDesk administrator connects a WhatsApp Business number for you. Once it's connected, the click-to-chat link and QR code appear here.
whatsapp.linkHint: Put this link on your website, emails and social profiles. It opens a WhatsApp chat with your business.
whatsapp.windowNote: WhatsApp rule: you can reply freely within 24 hours of the customer's last message. After that, they need to message you first.
whatsapp.qrHint: Print it on flyers, menus or your shop window. Scanning it opens a chat with you.

whatsappAdmin.title: WhatsApp numbers
whatsappAdmin.hint: Connect a WhatsApp Business number from your Meta app (WhatsApp → API setup shows its Phone number ID) to a business.
whatsappAdmin.notConfigured: WhatsApp isn't configured on this server (WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN, WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET and WHATSAPP_VERIFY_TOKEN in .env).
whatsappAdmin.confirmRemove: Disconnect this WhatsApp number? Messages to it will no longer be answered.

email.title: Email
email.subtitle: Connect your support mailbox. The assistant reads new emails, drafts a reply in your business's voice and puts it in the Inbox. You approve it, or let simple answers go out on their own.
email.noEncryptionKey: Mailbox passwords are stored encrypted, so SETTINGS_ENCRYPTION_KEY must be set in .env first.
email.lastChecked: Last checked {when}. New mail is checked every minute.
email.notCheckedYet: Not checked yet. New mail is checked every minute.
email.modeAuto: Simple answers are sent straight away. Complaints, cancellations and anything the assistant isn't sure about wait for you in the Inbox.
email.modeReview: Every reply waits in the Inbox for you to approve.
email.testOk: Logged in to the mailbox successfully.
email.confirmDisconnect: Disconnect this mailbox? The stored password is deleted and new emails won't be answered.
email.connectHint: Only emails that arrive after you connect are answered; older mail is left alone. Newsletters and automatic emails are ignored.
email.passwordKeep: Leave empty to keep the saved one
email.appPasswordHint: Use an app password, not your normal password. In Gmail: turn on 2-Step Verification, then Google Account → Security → App passwords. Microsoft 365 mailboxes aren't supported yet.
email.modeReviewOption: I approve every reply (recommended to start)
email.modeAutoOption: Send simple answers automatically; I approve the rest
email.connected: Mailbox connected. New emails will appear in the Inbox.

forms.title: Forms
forms.subtitle: Enquiries from your website forms land in the Inbox. The assistant reads each one, creates the right record (booking request, message or ticket) and drafts a reply for you to approve.
forms.statusHint: While it's off, the hosted form and the webhook don't accept submissions.
forms.hostedHint: A ready-made contact form. Link to it from your website, social profiles or emails.
forms.webhook: Connect a form you already have
forms.webhookHint: Point your form tool's webhook (Typeform, Jotform, Webflow, Tally, WordPress…) at this address. JSON and normal form posts both work.
forms.tunnelHint: While VoiceDesk runs on your computer, use the public address that pnpm tunnel prints. Keep the secret private: anyone with it can send enquiries.
forms.confirmRegenerate: Create a new form address and webhook secret? The old link and webhook stop working straight away.
forms.mappingHint: Leave empty to detect them automatically (fields called name, email, phone, message…). If your form has a consent box, enter its field name: without the tick, no reply is emailed.

hostedForm.name: Your name
hostedForm.needContact: Please give an email address or a phone number so we can reply.
hostedForm.consent: I agree that {business} may contact me about this enquiry.
hostedForm.marketing: I'd also like news and offers from {business} (optional).
hostedForm.aiNote: Your enquiry is read by an AI assistant and the team.

vas.title: VAs
vas.subtitle: People who answer calls handed over by the assistant, across businesses. Businesses can also let their own members answer calls (Team page).
vas.addTitle: Assign a VA to a business
vas.addHint: The person needs a VoiceDesk account first. Assigning makes them staff of that business, so they can see its calls, chats and contacts.

va.title: VA console
va.notAvailableHint: Calls only ring here while you're Available. Keep this tab open.
va.notAnswerer: You don't answer calls for any business yet
va.notAnswererHint: A business owner can switch on "Answers calls" for you on their Team page, or your VoiceDesk administrator can assign you as a VA.
va.chatsHint: Website chat, WhatsApp, email and form conversations where the customer asked for a person or the assistant needs help.
va.callsHint: Phone callers the assistant is connecting to a person. The first person to answer gets the call; the others stop ringing.
va.handBackHint: Hand back when you're done but the caller may still need something: the assistant tells them they're back with the AI assistant and carries on.
va.dialHint: The customer sees the business's number. Calls cost money at the phone provider and only go out once outbound calling is set up. Unsolicited calls only between 8am and 9pm.
va.dialCallback: They asked us to call back
va.outboundNote: Outbound calls aren't transcribed or recorded yet. Note anything important on the contact.
va.keepOpenHint: Keep this tab open while you're available: leaving it (or closing the laptop) makes you offline within a minute, and calls then go to your backup number or the assistant takes a message.
va.noMicrophone: No microphone found. Plug in a headset or microphone, then hang up and try again. You can still hear the other person.
va.micBlocked: The browser isn't allowed to use your microphone. Click the icon left of the web address, set Microphone to Allow, then hang up and try again.
va.notAnswered: The call didn't connect: nobody answered, or the phone company refused it. Hang up and try again.

feedbackSettings.title: Customer feedback
feedbackSettings.hint: At the end of a conversation the customer is asked one quick question ("How did we do?", 1–5). Nobody is asked more than once a month. Low scores alert you straight away.
feedbackSettings.enabled: Ask for a rating at the end of website chats and WhatsApp conversations, and by email after email or form enquiries (free)
feedbackSettings.afterCalls: Also text callers a rating link after phone calls (texts cost money)

feedback.title: Customer feedback
feedback.subtitle: How customers rate their conversations with your assistant and your team.
feedback.csatHint: Share of ratings that were 4 or 5 out of 5
feedback.empty: No ratings yet. They appear here as customers answer.

ratePage.title: How did we do?
ratePage.thanks: Thank you! Your feedback goes straight to {business}.
ratePage.answered: You've already rated this conversation. Thank you!

dailyBrief.title: Daily brief
dailyBrief.hint: Every morning at 07:30 your time, owners and admins get one email: yesterday's calls, chats, bookings and issues, today's bookings, and anything waiting for you.

aiCalls.title: Calls the assistant makes
aiCalls.hint: The assistant can phone customers itself, always introducing itself as an AI. It needs outbound calling set up for your number, and calls cost money at your phone provider.
aiCalls.callbacks: Call customers back when they ask for a callback
aiCalls.confirmations: Phone to confirm bookings (instead of the reminder text)
aiCalls.rules: Only between 8am and 9pm your time, never to customers marked “Don't phone”, at most two attempts per call. If nobody answers it leaves a short voicemail with your number.

ask.title: Ask VoiceDesk
ask.subtitle: Ask about your bookings, calls, messages and customers, or ask it to do something. It prepares changes for you to approve; nothing happens without your click.
ask.example2: Which messages haven't been dealt with, and what do they want?
ask.example3: Draft a reply to the WhatsApp customer waiting for us.
ask.placeholder: Ask a question or say what you need…
ask.noAnswer: I couldn't find an answer to that.
ask.privacy: Answers come only from your own VoiceDesk data. Questions are processed by the AI provider switched on for your account.

design.title: Design system
design.description: Every token and component of Aurora Glow, in dark and light.

setup.title: Setup
setup.subtitle: What works on this server today, and exactly what each feature still needs. Settings go in the .env file; restart VoiceDesk after changing it.

ai.name: AI provider
ai.unlocks: The assistant's brain: chat, calls, summaries and Ask VoiceDesk.
ai.how: Platform admin → AI providers: switch on DeepSeek or Claude and add its API key.

voice.name: Voice
voice.unlocks: Talking to the assistant: speech recognition, natural voices and live calls in the browser.
voice.how: Add the LiveKit, Deepgram and ElevenLabs keys to .env.

phone.name: Phone calls
phone.unlocks: Customers ringing a business's phone number and reaching the assistant.
phone.how: Set SIP_AUTH_USERNAME and SIP_AUTH_PASSWORD in .env, then add the number under Phone numbers.

email.name: Real emails
email.unlocks: Sign-up verification, invitations, call summaries, the daily brief and email replies reach real inboxes. Until then they appear in Mailpit (localhost:8025).
email.how: Use an email-sending service (Brevo or Resend have free tiers, or Gmail with an app password). Put its SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORT, SMTP_USER, SMTP_PASSWORD and an EMAIL_FROM address you own in .env.

sms.name: Text messages
sms.unlocks: Booking confirmations, reminders and feedback links by SMS. Until then texts appear in Mailpit.
sms.how: Set SMS_PROVIDER=twilio (or telnyx), that carrier's API keys, and SMS_FROM: a number that can send texts.

googleCalendar.name: Google Calendar
googleCalendar.unlocks: Bookings check a business's Google Calendar for free times and add events to it.
googleCalendar.how: In Google Cloud Console create an OAuth client (Web application) with the redirect URI {origin}/api/integrations/google/callback, then set GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID and GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET.

microsoftCalendar.name: Outlook / Microsoft 365
microsoftCalendar.unlocks: The same as Google Calendar, for businesses on Outlook.
microsoftCalendar.how: In Microsoft Entra (Azure) register an app with the redirect URI {origin}/api/integrations/microsoft/callback and a client secret, then set MICROSOFT_CLIENT_ID and MICROSOFT_CLIENT_SECRET.

mailbox.name: Email inbox
mailbox.unlocks: The assistant reads a business's mailbox, answers simple emails and drafts the rest for approval.
mailbox.how: Each business connects its own mailbox on its Email page, using an app password. The server only needs SETTINGS_ENCRYPTION_KEY.

whatsapp.name: WhatsApp
whatsapp.unlocks: Customers chat with the assistant on WhatsApp.
whatsapp.how: Create a Meta developer app with the WhatsApp product, then set WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN, WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET and WHATSAPP_VERIFY_TOKEN. While VoiceDesk runs on this computer, run pnpm tunnel so Meta can reach it.

outbound.name: Outbound calls
outbound.unlocks: The assistant calls customers back, confirms bookings by phone, and VAs dial out.
outbound.how: Create a SIP trunk for outgoing calls (Twilio Elastic SIP Trunking, or a Telnyx credentials connection) and set its SIP_OUTBOUND_* login in .env.

publicAddress.name: Public web address
publicAddress.unlocks: Website chat on real websites, and hosted forms and rating links that customers can open.
publicAddress.how: Host VoiceDesk on a server with your own domain (part of Phase 7). Until then it runs on this computer only.

help.title: VoiceDesk Help
help.subtitle: Answers about using VoiceDesk
help.intro: Hi! Ask me anything about VoiceDesk: setting something up, fixing a problem, or getting more out of it.
help.articlesMode: AI answers are off, so here are the matching help articles.
help.contactHint: Tell us what's wrong or what you need. We'll reply by email.
help.privacy: Answers come from VoiceDesk help. Don't share customers' personal details here.
help.error: Help isn't available right now. Please try again.

supportRequests.title: Support requests
supportRequests.subtitle: Questions people sent with Contact support in the Help assistant. Reply by email, then mark them resolved.
supportRequests.emptyHint: When someone uses Contact support in the Help assistant, it appears here and is emailed to you.

mfa.title: Turn on two-step login
mfa.subtitle: A code from your phone, as well as your password, keeps your business safe.
mfa.why: Two-step login is required for business owners, admins and the platform owner to use admin features. Set it up below with an authenticator app (for example Google Authenticator or Microsoft Authenticator).
mfa.done: Two-step login is on. You can use every feature again.

reauth.title: Confirm it's you
reauth.description: Enter your password to make this change. You won't be asked again for 5 minutes.
reauth.tooMany: Too many tries. Please wait a minute and try again.
